text:
maya: Dropping a new prototype for the first-run surface — this one is a compact inline strip that expands into a lightweight walkthrough. Goal: reduce modal interruptions and keep users in context. Can folks poke for UX, copy, and accessibility issues? :wave:

lucy: Visual feedback: the inline strip reads lighter than the surrounding page; it gets lost on busy dashboards. Proposal: subtle card shadow + 2px separator line to anchor it. Also thinking of adding a small numbered step pill (1/3) to indicate progression.

ryan: Technical constraints: adding a persistent strip means we need to avoid focus traps. Current implementation traps focus when expanded; I'll change it so expansion is not modal, and tab order follows page content. For keyboard users, pressing ESC should collapse the strip (not close the whole drawer).

jin: A11y callouts: when the strip expands we need to announce "Onboarding step 1 of 3: create API key" with role=region and aria-live=polite. Also ensure the expand/collapse control is `button[aria-expanded]` and visible focus styles are present. We should not rely on color alone — include an icon + text.

nora: Copy tweaks: current header says "Start with a sample" which is vague. Suggest: "Run a sample project or create an API key" as the primary line and then a second line: "Pick a template to try Redwood quickly" as supporting text. For the step pill, use verbs: "Step 1: Create key" rather than numbers only.

lucy: Good idea. Also we should surface thumbnail alt text for each template preview: e.g., `alt="Todo sample app UI screenshot"`. If we include animated GIFs for templates, make sure there's a pause control and `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.

ryan: Note on disabled states: if user has no billing or account verification, the "Run sample" CTA should be disabled with tooltip explaining why. Avoid hidden CTA that fails later. Tooltip content: "Verify your account to run hosted samples".

jin: Contrast check: the CTA on the strip uses a gradient that falls to 3.9:1 over white on some screens. Please switch to solid color or tweak text weight to meet 4.5:1 for normal text. Also ensure focus ring is at least 3px and uses a color with sufficient contrast.

maya: Measurement plan: we want to measure two variants — compact inline strip (this prototype) vs a small persistent button that opens an unfolding panel. Hypothesis: strip will convert more but might be ignored on dense pages. Ryan, can you add experiment flags?

ryan: Yep — will add feature flag `onboard.first_run_variant` with values `inline_strip` and `unfold_panel`. Events: `first_run.view`, `first_run.expand`, `first_run.complete_step` with payload { variant, step, user_id }. Keep payload minimal.

nora: Privacy note: we should show a one-line telemetry hint in the strip footer: "We collect anonymous usage to improve onboarding — manage in Settings." Keep link to privacy settings. Avoid legal-heavy language.

lucy: UX microflow: when user collapses the strip, do not show it again for 24 hours. If user completes any onboarding action (create key, run sample), dismiss permanently. Persist state server-side for signed-in users; localStorage fallback for guests.

jin: For screen readers, when the user navigates back to the dashboard, if the strip is collapsed we should not auto-expand. Auto-expanding can be disorienting. Only expand on explicit action or first sign-in.

ryan: Deployed preview -> https://preview.redwood-inference/internal/first-run/1965432102 (build 2026-03-23-88). Please test keyboard + mobile.

maya: Action items: lucy -> refine visual anchor + thumbnails + motion handling; jin -> aria-live/announce text + focus styles; ryan -> feature flag + telemetry + non-modal keyboard flow + disabled tooltips; nora -> final copy and tiny telemetry hint. Reconvene tomorrow after quick AXE pass. :thumbsup:
